back:
The compiler reports the line it was compiling when it noticed the problem, not always the line where you would conventionally put the missing token.

A missing semicolon is the classic case: some compilers flag the next line (e.g. return) instead of the statement that needed the semicolon. If the marked line looks fine, check the previous line.
